$description: DateTimeInput V2 Component Contract. One public temporal-input identity with a custom field and calendar popup shell; Qt native temporal types remain value and parsing adapters only.

stateLayers.mode: date, time or datetime editor capability
stateLayers.focus: keyboard-only border focus ring; popup cells use their own focus indication
stateLayers.availability: disabled, error and loading lock interaction
stateLayers.content: runtime date/time value and locale-formatted sections
stateLayers.calendarSelection: single or range selection is runtime behavior, not a DateTimeInput visual axis

figmaEvidence.note: The Figma source demonstrates a custom calendar grid, range segments, month navigation and popup actions; native Qt editor visuals are not the design source.

eventBoundary.inputs: QDate/QTime/QDateTime-compatible values and native editor events
eventBoundary.outputs: native value-change, editing, validation and commit notifications

compositionRules: DateTimeInput is the public semantic identity; DatePicker, TimePicker and DateTimePicker are legacy aliases, not parallel public visual components.

Field content uses Runtime locale formatting for display but remains section-editable with native temporal-editor semantics: date fields expose year/month/day sections, time fields expose hour/minute/second sections, and datetime fields combine both. Section navigation and adjustment change only the temporary value until confirmation.

An empty DateTimeInput renders localized placeholder content using the active state text color; it does not create a placeholder-specific color token. If the optional clear action is enabled, clearing sets only the temporary value to null; when the popup is closed it opens for confirmation, and when already open it remains open until confirm or cancel.

Locale, date order, separators and display format are Runtime content behavior; the time presentation remains 24-hour-only. Partial section input may remain temporarily visible with section placeholders, but confirmation is blocked until the complete value passes Runtime validation.

DateTimeInput focus lifecycle is unified across date, time, datetime and range modes: opening moves focus from the field to the active popup target; keyboard navigation remains within the active popup surface; confirm commits and returns focus to the field; cancel, Escape and outside-click discard the temporary value and return focus to the field.
Qt QDate/QTime/QDateTime and the native editor classes provide temporal values, parsing, formatting and keyboard stepping only; they do not define the final visual shell.
Date mode may expose a calendar action; time and datetime modes may expose spin sections. The field shell and popup shell remain project-owned and share one Token contract.
The calendar popup is a private composition of header, weekday row, day grid, range overlay, navigation buttons and action buttons. It is not a second public component identity in this slice.

Date range uses the same DateTimeInput identity with Runtime selectionMode=range; RangeFields expresses start/end content, renders the same date in both fields for a same-day range, exposes an empty end field and disabled confirmation in start-only state, and clears the old end when the user reselects the start. CalendarSurface expresses the selection interaction, and ActionArea expresses popup commit or cancellation actions.

Multiple selection uses the same DateTimeInput identity with Runtime selectionMode=multiple; each date click toggles a temporary date across months, never auto-creates a range, and only confirmation commits the complete set.
Single selection uses the same temporary-value lifecycle; selecting one date does not auto-close or auto-commit, and confirmation is required.
Adjacent-month dates may remain visible in the square day grid with the out-of-month visual state, but are not selectable unless Runtime explicitly enables cross-month selection.
After a range start is selected, hovering or keyboard-focusing a candidate end renders a preview-only range; leaving the candidate clears the preview without changing the temporary selection.
Minimum, maximum and disabled-date constraints keep dates visible with the disabled visual state while blocking pointer selection, keyboard selection and range submission.
A range that contains an unavailable date shows a SelectionHint error and disables confirmation until the temporary range is valid.
When the range end precedes the range start, the system does not auto-swap the dates; it shows a SelectionHint error and disables confirmation.
When the range start and end are the same date, the range is valid and commits as a single-day range.
Clicking a selected range start or end re-enters endpoint editing; Runtime recomputes the temporary range and preview from the edited endpoint.
Clicking a date inside the selected range starts a new temporary range from that date, clears the old end, and returns RangeFields to start-only.

Calendar keyboard navigation uses arrow keys for day focus, Enter/Space for temporary selection, PageUp/PageDown for month navigation, and Escape to discard and return focus to the field. Month navigation preserves the temporary selection and range preview.

The year header opens a contextual year-selection surface inside CalendarSurface; it is not a separate public YearPicker component or DateTimeInput axis. Changing the year preserves the temporary selection and range preview.
Year selection uses arrow keys to move the focused candidate, Enter/Space to set the temporary year, and Escape to return focus to YearHeader without discarding the date-time temporary value.

Year options are a private CalendarSurface slot that reuses shared text, selected, focused and disabled semantic tokens; no public YearOption component or independent token family is created. Their visual priority is disabled, selected, focused, hover, then default.

Month selection uses a private contextual month grid inside CalendarSurface; it is not a public MonthPicker component or an independent DateTimeInput axis. The grid contains the twelve months of the selected year. Selecting a month returns to the month/day grid within the same popup and preserves the temporary value and range preview. Months with no selectable date remain visible but disabled and keyboard-focusable, with Enter/Space as a no-op.

Time and datetime modes may use the private TimeWheelSurface. The field or time action opens it and focus enters the active time item. Wheel, drag and arrow-key changes all snap to the active step; non-step values are rejected. The temporary 24-hour time value uses second precision; Runtime may select a step of 1, 5, 10, 30 or 60 seconds. Confirm commits and returns focus to the field; cancel, Escape and outside-click discard the temporary value and return focus to the field. Disabled, Error and Loading cannot open the popup. AM/PM and 12-hour presentation are not supported.
Popup open/close, calendar selection, locale, range constraints, seconds and AM/PM display are Runtime API behavior, not Component Token axes.
Focused uses a border-only focus ring. ReadOnly uses the disabled visual and locks editing. Error and Loading also lock interaction; Loading uses the shared Spinner.
